topics: Law of Sines, Law of Cosines & Heron's formula

body.en: Advanced Euclidean geometry represents roughly 10% of the EST II Math Level 1 exam. Candidates must master rigorous angle relationships with parallel lines and transversals, prove and apply triangle similarity and congruence criteria, apply the Law of Cosines and Law of Sines to non-right (oblique) triangles, compute areas using sine-area and Heron's formulas, and analyze regular polygon apothems and diagonals.
body.ar: Advanced Euclidean الهندسة represents roughly 10% of the EST II Math Level 1 exam. Candidates must master rigorous الزاوية relationships with parallel lines and transversals, prove and apply المثلث similarity and congruence criteria, apply the Law of Cosines and Law of Sines to non-right (oblique) triangles, compute areas using sine-المساحة and Heron's الصيغ, and analyze regular polygon apothems and diagonals.

label.en: Definition 4.1 — Transversals, Similarity, and Polygon Properties
label.ar: تعريف 4.1 — Transversals, Similarity, and Polygon Properties

body.en:
Core geometric definitions and structural angle relationships:
  • Parallel Lines and Transversals: Two parallel lines intersected by a transversal produce equal alternate interior, alternate exterior, and corresponding angles; consecutive interior angles are supplementary (sum to \(180^\circ\)).
  • Triangle Similarity & Congruence Criteria:
    1. Congruence (\(\cong\)): SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, and HL (Hypotenuse-Leg for right triangles). All corresponding sides and angles are equal.
    2. Similarity (\(\sim\)): AA (Angle-Angle), SAS similarity, and SSS similarity. Corresponding angles are equal; corresponding sides are in constant ratio \(k\).
  • Polygon Formulas: For a convex polygon with \(n\) vertices:
    1. Interior angle sum: \(S_{\text{int}} = (n - 2) \times 180^\circ\).
    2. Each interior angle of a regular \(n\)-gon: \(\theta_{\text{int}} = \frac{(n - 2) \times 180^\circ}{n} = 180^\circ - \frac{360^\circ}{n}\).
    3. Exterior angle sum: \(S_{\text{ext}} = 360^\circ\) (each exterior angle is \(\frac{360^\circ}{n}\)).
    4. Number of distinct diagonals: \(D = \frac{n(n - 3)}{2}\).
    5. Area of a regular polygon: \(A = \frac{1}{2} a P\), where \(a\) is the apothem and \(P\) is the perimeter.
body.ar:
Core geometric definitions and structural الزاوية relationships:
  • Parallel Lines and Transversals: Two parallel lines intersected by a transversal produce equal alternate interior, alternate exterior, and corresponding angles; consecutive interior angles are supplementary (sum to \(180^\circ\)).
  • Triangle Similarity & Congruence Criteria:
    1. Congruence (\(\cong\)): SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, and HL (Hypotenuse-Leg for right triangles). All corresponding sides and angles are equal.
    2. Similarity (\(\sim\)): AA (الزاوية-الزاوية), SAS similarity, and SSS similarity. Corresponding angles are equal; corresponding sides are in الثابت ratio \(k\).
  • Polygon الصيغ: For a convex polygon with \(n\) vertices:
    1. Interior الزاوية sum: \(S_{\text{int}} = (n - 2) \times 180^\circ\).
    2. Each interior الزاوية of a regular \(n\)-gon: \(\theta_{\text{int}} = \frac{(n - 2) \times 180^\circ}{n} = 180^\circ - \frac{360^\circ}{n}\).
    3. Exterior الزاوية sum: \(S_{\text{ext}} = 360^\circ\) (each exterior الزاوية is \(\frac{360^\circ}{n}\)).
    4. Number of distinct diagonals: \(D = \frac{n(n - 3)}{2}\).
    5. المساحة of a regular polygon: \(A = \frac{1}{2} a P\), حيث \(a\) is the apothem and \(P\) is the المحيط.

label.en: ● Deep Conceptual Intuition — Lines, Triangles & Polygons
label.ar: ● الحدس المفاهيمي العميق — Lines, Triangles & Polygons

body.en: Euclidean Invariants, Locus Equations & Scaling Laws: In analytic geometry, geometric loci translate into algebraic constraints via Euclidean distance \(d = \sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2 + (y_2-y_1)^2}\). A circle of center \((h, k)\) and radius \(r\) satisfies \((x-h)^2 + (y-k)^2 = r^2\), and a tangent line at point \(P\) is strictly perpendicular to the radius \(CP\) (\(m_{\text{tan}} \cdot m_{\text{rad}} = -1\)). Under a similarity scale factor \(k\), all linear lengths scale by \(k\), surface areas scale by \(k^2\), and volumes scale by \(k^3\).
body.ar: Euclidean Invariants, Locus المعادلات & Scaling Laws: In analytic الهندسة, geometric loci translate into algebraic constraints via Euclidean distance \(d = \sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2 + (y_2-y_1)^2}\). A الدائرة of center \((h, k)\) and نصف القطر \(r\) satisfies \((x-h)^2 + (y-k)^2 = r^2\), and a خط المماس at point \(P\) is strictly perpendicular to the نصف القطر \(CP\) (\(m_{\text{tan}} \cdot m_{\text{rad}} = -1\)). Under a similarity scale factor \(k\), all linear lengths scale by \(k\), surface areas scale by \(k^2\), and volumes scale by \(k^3\).

label.en: Theorem 4.1 — Exterior Angle Theorem, Law of Cosines, and Heron's Formula
label.ar: مبرهنة 4.1 — Exterior الزاوية مبرهنة, Law of Cosines, and Heron's الصيغة

body.en:
Fundamental theorems for general triangles and polygon mensuration:
  • Exterior Angle Theorem: An exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two non-adjacent (remote) interior angles:
    \[ \theta_{\text{ext}} = \angle A + \angle B \]
  • Triangle Inequality Theorem: In any non-degenerate triangle with side lengths \(a, b, c\):
    \[ |a - b| < c < a + b \]
  • Law of Cosines (for any oblique triangle):
    \[ c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab \cos C \implies \cos C = \frac{a^2 + b^2 - c^2}{2ab} \]
  • Heron's Formula: For a triangle with side lengths \(a, b, c\) and semi-perimeter \(s = \frac{a + b + c}{2}\):
    \[ \text{Area} = \sqrt{s(s - a)(s - b)(s - c)} \]
body.ar:
Fundamental theorems for general triangles and polygon mensuration:
  • Exterior الزاوية مبرهنة: An exterior الزاوية of a المثلث equals the sum of the two non-adjacent (remote) interior angles:
    \[ \theta_{\text{ext}} = \angle A + \angle B \]
  • Triangle المتباينة مبرهنة: In any non-degenerate المثلث with side lengths \(a, b, c\):
    \[ |a - b| < c < a + b \]
  • Law of Cosines (for any oblique المثلث):
    \[ c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab \cos C \implies \cos C = \frac{a^2 + b^2 - c^2}{2ab} \]
  • Heron's الصيغة: For a المثلث with side lengths \(a, b, c\) and semi-المحيط \(s = \frac{a + b + c}{2}\):
    \[ \text{Area} = \sqrt{s(s - a)(s - b)(s - c)} \]

label.en: ▲ EST II Math Traps & Pitfalls — Triangles, Polygons & Area
label.ar: ▲ EST II Math Traps & Pitfalls — Triangles, Polygons & المساحة

body.en:
• Linear vs. Area vs. Volume Scale Factors: If two similar polygons have a linear scale factor of \(k\), their perimeters scale by \(k\), but their areas scale by \(k^2\). On EST II, questions often provide the ratio of areas (e.g. \(9:16\)) and ask for perimeter — take the square root (\(3:4\)) first!
  • Regular Polygon Angle Inversions: Interior angle is \(\frac{(n-2)180°}{n}\), while exterior angle is \(\frac{360°}{n}\). Notice that \(\text{interior} + \text{exterior} = 180°\). It is almost always faster to compute the exterior angle first and subtract from \(180°\).
  • Triangle Inequality Theorem: For any valid triangle with sides \(a, b, c\), the sum of any two sides must be strictly greater than the third: \(a + b > c\), \(a + c > b\), \(b + c > a\). This implies \(|a - b| < c < a + b\).
  • Heron's Formula vs. Trigonometric Area: If all 3 sides are known, use Heron's formula: \(A = \sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)}\) where semi-perimeter \(s = \frac{a+b+c}{2}\). If two sides and included angle are known, use \(\frac{1}{2}ab\sin C\).
body.ar:
• Linear vs. المساحة vs. الحجم Scale Factors: If two similar polygons have a linear scale factor of \(k\), their perimeters scale by \(k\), but their areas scale by \(k^2\). On EST II, questions often provide the ratio of areas (e.g. \(9:16\)) and ask for المحيط — take the square root (\(3:4\)) first!
  • Regular Polygon الزاوية Inversions: Interior الزاوية is \(\frac{(n-2)180°}{n}\), while exterior الزاوية is \(\frac{360°}{n}\). Notice that \(\text{interior} + \text{exterior} = 180°\). It is almost always faster to compute the exterior الزاوية first and subtract from \(180°\).
  • Triangle المتباينة مبرهنة: For any valid المثلث with sides \(a, b, c\), the sum of any two sides must be strictly greater than the third: \(a + b > c\), \(a + c > b\), \(b + c > a\). This implies \(|a - b| < c < a + b\).
  • Heron's الصيغة vs. Trigonometric المساحة: If all 3 sides are known, use Heron's الصيغة: \(A = \sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)}\) حيث semi-المحيط \(s = \frac{a+b+c}{2}\). If two sides and included الزاوية are known, use \(\frac{1}{2}ab\sin C\).

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Lines, Triangles & Polygons)
label.ar: ◆ لماذا تعمل هذه الطريقة رياضياً — First-Principles اشتقاق (Lines, Triangles & Polygons)

body.en:
Why Inscribed Angles Equal Half the Central Angle & Circle Completion Works: Given \(x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\), completing the square in \(x\) and \(y\) simultaneously yields:

\[ (x + g)^2 - g^2 + (y + f)^2 - f^2 + c = 0 \implies (x + g)^2 + (y + f)^2 = g^2 + f^2 - c \]

Thus the center is \((-g, -f)\) and the radius is \(r = \sqrt{g^2 + f^2 - c}\) (requiring \(g^2 + f^2 > c\)). In any circle, drawing diameter \(POQ\) splits an inscribed angle \(\angle APB\) into two isosceles triangles \(\triangle OAP\) and \(\triangle OBP\) (since \(OA = OB = OP = r\)); by the exterior angle theorem, \(\angle AOB = 2\angle APB\).
body.ar:
Why Inscribed Angles Equal Half the Central الزاوية & الدائرة Completion Works: المعطيات \(x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\), completing the square in \(x\) and \(y\) simultaneously yields:

\[ (x + g)^2 - g^2 + (y + f)^2 - f^2 + c = 0 \implies (x + g)^2 + (y + f)^2 = g^2 + f^2 - c \]

Thus the center is \((-g, -f)\) and the نصف القطر is \(r = \sqrt{g^2 + f^2 - c}\) (requiring \(g^2 + f^2 > c\)). In any الدائرة, drawing القطر \(POQ\) splits an inscribed الزاوية \(\angle APB\) into two isosceles triangles \(\triangle OAP\) and \(\triangle OBP\) (since \(OA = OB = OP = r\)); by the exterior الزاوية المبرهنة, \(\angle AOB = 2\angle APB\).

label.en: Worked Example 4.A — Oblique Triangle Solution via Law of Cosines
label.ar: مثال محلول 4.A — Oblique المثلث الحل via Law of Cosines

body.en:
In triangle \(ABC\), side \(a = 7\text{ cm}\), side \(b = 10\text{ cm}\), and included angle \(C = 60^\circ\).
(a) Find the exact length of side \(c\).
(b) Calculate the exact area of triangle \(ABC\).

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. (a) Apply the Law of Cosines:
    \[ c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab \cos C \]
    Substitute values with \(\cos 60^\circ = 0.5\):
    \[ c^2 = 7^2 + 10^2 - 2(7)(10)\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = 49 + 100 - 70 = 79 \]
    Taking the square root gives:
    \[ c = \mathbf{\sqrt{79}\text{ cm}} \approx 8.89\text{ cm} \]
  2. (b) Calculate the area using sine formula:
    \[ \text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} a b \sin C = \frac{1}{2}(7)(10)\sin(60^\circ) = 35 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = \mathbf{\frac{35\sqrt{3}}{2}\text{ cm}^2} \approx 30.31\text{ cm}^2 \]
body.ar:
In المثلث \(ABC\), side \(a = 7\text{ cm}\), side \(b = 10\text{ cm}\), and included الزاوية \(C = 60^\circ\).
(a) أوجد exact length of side \(c\).
(b) احسب exact المساحة of المثلث \(ABC\).

Step-by-step الحل:
  1. (a) Apply the Law of Cosines:
    \[ c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab \cos C \]
    Substitute values with \(\cos 60^\circ = 0.5\):
    \[ c^2 = 7^2 + 10^2 - 2(7)(10)\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = 49 + 100 - 70 = 79 \]
    Taking the square root gives:
    \[ c = \mathbf{\sqrt{79}\text{ cm}} \approx 8.89\text{ cm} \]
  2. (b) احسب المساحة using sine الصيغة:
    \[ \text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} a b \sin C = \frac{1}{2}(7)(10)\sin(60^\circ) = 35 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = \mathbf{\frac{35\sqrt{3}}{2}\text{ cm}^2} \approx 30.31\text{ cm}^2 \]

label.en: Worked Example 4.B — Regular Polygon Apothem & Area Analysis
label.ar: مثال محلول 4.B — Regular Polygon Apothem & المساحة Analysis

body.en:
A regular hexagon is inscribed in a circle of radius \(R = 8\text{ cm}\).
(a) Determine the apothem \(a\) of the hexagon.
(b) Compute the exact area of the hexagon.
(c) Calculate the exact area of the region inside the circle but outside the hexagon.

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. (a) Find side length and apothem:
    In a regular hexagon, side length equals circumradius: \(s = R = 8\text{ cm}\).
    The apothem is the height of an equilateral triangle with side length 8:
    \[ a = s \cos(30^\circ) = 8 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = \mathbf{4\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}} \]
  2. (b) Compute hexagon area:
    Perimeter is \(P = 6 \times 8 = 48\text{ cm}\):
    \[ A_{\text{hex}} = \frac{1}{2} a P = \frac{1}{2}(4\sqrt{3})(48) = \mathbf{96\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2} \approx 166.28\text{ cm}^2 \]
  3. (c) Shaded region area:
    Area of circle is \(A_{\text{circle}} = \pi R^2 = \pi (8^2) = 64\pi\text{ cm}^2\).
    \[ A_{\text{region}} = A_{\text{circle}} - A_{\text{hex}} = \mathbf{64\pi - 96\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2} \approx 34.78\text{ cm}^2 \]
body.ar:
A regular hexagon is inscribed in a الدائرة of نصف القطر \(R = 8\text{ cm}\).
(a) حدّد apothem \(a\) of the hexagon.
(b) Compute the exact المساحة of the hexagon.
(c) احسب exact المساحة of the region inside the الدائرة but outside the hexagon.

Step-by-step الحل:
  1. (a) Find side length and apothem:
    In a regular hexagon, side length equals circumradius: \(s = R = 8\text{ cm}\).
    The apothem is the height of an equilateral المثلث with side length 8:
    \[ a = s \cos(30^\circ) = 8 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = \mathbf{4\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}} \]
  2. (b) Compute hexagon المساحة:
    Perimeter is \(P = 6 \times 8 = 48\text{ cm}\):
    \[ A_{\text{hex}} = \frac{1}{2} a P = \frac{1}{2}(4\sqrt{3})(48) = \mathbf{96\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2} \approx 166.28\text{ cm}^2 \]
  3. (c) Shaded region المساحة:
    Area of الدائرة is \(A_{\text{circle}} = \pi R^2 = \pi (8^2) = 64\pi\text{ cm}^2\).
    \[ A_{\text{region}} = A_{\text{circle}} - A_{\text{hex}} = \mathbf{64\pi - 96\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2} \approx 34.78\text{ cm}^2 \]

label.en: Worked Example 4.C — Triangle Inequality & Integer Side Constraints
label.ar: مثال محلول 4.C — المثلث المتباينة & Integer Side Constraints

body.en:
Two sides of an obtuse triangle have lengths 6 and 9. If the third side \(x\) is an integer, determine the number of possible values for \(x\).

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Apply the Triangle Inequality Theorem:
    For any triangle with sides 6, 9, and \(x\):
    \[ |9 - 6| < x < 9 + 6 \implies 3 < x < 15 \]
  2. Apply the Obtuse Triangle Criteria:
    A triangle is obtuse if \(c^2 > a^2 + b^2\) where \(c\) is the longest side:
    Case 1: 9 is the longest side (\(x \le 9\)):
    \[ 9^2 > 6^2 + x^2 \implies 81 > 36 + x^2 \implies x^2 < 45 \implies x < \sqrt{45} \approx 6.71 \]
    Integer values satisfying \(3 < x < 6.71\) are \(x = 4, 5, 6\).
    Case 2: \(x\) is the longest side (\(x > 9\)):
    \[ x^2 > 6^2 + 9^2 = 36 + 81 = 117 \implies x > \sqrt{117} \approx 10.82 \]
    Integer values satisfying \(10.82 < x < 15\) are \(x = 11, 12, 13, 14\).
  3. Combine valid integer values:
    Possible values of \(x\) are \(\{4, 5, 6, 11, 12, 13, 14\}\).
    There are exactly 7 possible integer values.
body.ar:
Two sides of an obtuse المثلث have lengths 6 and 9. If the third side \(x\) is an integer, حدّد number of possible values for \(x\).

Step-by-step الحل:
  1. Apply the المثلث المتباينة مبرهنة:
    For any المثلث with sides 6, 9, and \(x\):
    \[ |9 - 6| < x < 9 + 6 \implies 3 < x < 15 \]
  2. Apply the Obtuse المثلث Criteria:
    A المثلث is obtuse if \(c^2 > a^2 + b^2\) حيث \(c\) is the longest side:
    Case 1: 9 is the longest side (\(x \le 9\)):
    \[ 9^2 > 6^2 + x^2 \implies 81 > 36 + x^2 \implies x^2 < 45 \implies x < \sqrt{45} \approx 6.71 \]
    Integer values satisfying \(3 < x < 6.71\) are \(x = 4, 5, 6\).
    Case 2: \(x\) is the longest side (\(x > 9\)):
    \[ x^2 > 6^2 + 9^2 = 36 + 81 = 117 \implies x > \sqrt{117} \approx 10.82 \]
    Integer values satisfying \(10.82 < x < 15\) are \(x = 11, 12, 13, 14\).
  3. Combine valid integer values:
    Possible values of \(x\) are \(\{4, 5, 6, 11, 12, 13, 14\}\).
    There are exactly 7 possible integer values.

label.en: Worked Example \(D\) — Lines, Triangles & Polygons (Hard Application)
label.ar: مثال محلول \(D\) — Lines, Triangles & Polygons (Hard Application)

body.en:
Problem (Hard): In the diagram, \( ABCD \) is a trapezoid with \( AB \parallel DC \). The diagonals \( AC \) and \( BD \) intersect at point \( E \). Given that \( AE = 3 \) cm, \( EC = 6 \) cm, and \( BE = 4 \) cm, find the length of \( BD \).

Step-by-Step Solution: Since \( AB \parallel DC \), we have that \( \triangle ABE \sim \triangle CDE \) (by AAA similarity, where \( \angle BAE = \angle DCE \) and \( \angle ABE = \angle CDE \) are alternate interior angles, and \( \angle AEB = \angle CED \) are vertically opposite angles). Therefore, the ratio of corresponding sides is equal: \( \frac{AE}{CE} = \frac{BE}{DE} = \frac{AB}{CD} \). We are given \( AE = 3 \) cm, \( EC = 6 \) cm, and \( BE = 4 \) cm. Plugging these values into the proportion, we get: \( \frac{3}{6} = \frac{4}{DE} \) This simplifies to \( \frac{1}{2} = \frac{4}{DE} \). Solving for \( DE \), we get \( DE = 2 \times 4 = 8 \) cm. The length of diagonal \( BD \) is the sum of the lengths of \( BE \) and \( DE \): \( BD = BE + DE = 4 + 8 = 12 \) cm.
body.ar:
Problem (Hard): In the المخطط, \( ABCD \) is a trapezoid with \( AB \parallel DC \). The diagonals \( AC \) and \( BD \) intersect at point \( E \). بما أن \( AE = 3 \) cm, \( EC = 6 \) cm, and \( BE = 4 \) cm, أوجد length of \( BD \).

Step-by-Step الحل: Since \( AB \parallel DC \), we have that \( \triangle ABE \sim \triangle CDE \) (by AAA similarity, حيث \( \angle BAE = \angle DCE \) and \( \angle ABE = \angle CDE \) are alternate interior angles, and \( \angle AEB = \angle CED \) are vertically opposite angles). وبالتالي, the ratio of corresponding sides is equal: \( \frac{AE}{CE} = \frac{BE}{DE} = \frac{AB}{CD} \). We are المعطيات \( AE = 3 \) cm, \( EC = 6 \) cm, and \( BE = 4 \) cm. Plugging these values into the proportion, we get: \( \frac{3}{6} = \frac{4}{DE} \) This simplifies to \( \frac{1}{2} = \frac{4}{DE} \). Solving for \( DE \), we get \( DE = 2 \times 4 = 8 \) cm. The length of diagonal \( BD \) is the sum of the lengths of \( BE \) and \( DE \): \( BD = BE + DE = 4 + 8 = 12 \) cm.

question.en: Two sides of a right triangle are 7 cm and 10 cm. If the third side is the hypotenuse, find: (a) the exact hypotenuse length, and (b) the measure of the smaller acute angle to the nearest tenth of a degree.
question.ar: Two sides of a right triangle are 7 cm and 10 cm. إذا كان the third side is the hypotenuse, أوجد: (a) the exact hypotenuse length, and (b) the measure of the smaller acute angle مقرباً إلى أقرب tenth of a degree.

solution.en:
(a) Exact hypotenuse: \[ c = \sqrt{7^2 + 10^2} = \sqrt{49 + 100} = \mathbf{\sqrt{149}\text{ cm}} \approx 12.21\text{ cm}. \]

(b) Smaller acute angle: The smaller angle is opposite the shorter leg (7 cm): \[ \tan\theta = \frac{7}{10} = 0.7 \implies \theta = \arctan(0.7) \approx \mathbf{35.0^\circ}. \]

question.en: A regular hexagon has side length \(s = 6\text{ cm}\). (a) Calculate the exact area of the hexagon. (b) Find the length of the long diagonal connecting two opposite vertices.
question.ar: A regular hexagon has side length \(s = 6\text{ cm}\). (a) احسب exact area of the hexagon. (b) أوجد length of the long diagonal connecting two opposite vertices.

solution.en:
(a) Exact area: A regular hexagon is composed of 6 congruent equilateral triangles of side length \(s = 6\). The area of one equilateral triangle is \(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}s^2 = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}(36) = 9\sqrt{3}\). Total area is: \[ A = 6 \times 9\sqrt{3} = \mathbf{54\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2} \approx 93.53\text{ cm}^2. \]

(b) Long diagonal: The long diagonal passes through the center of the circumscribed circle and equals twice the side length: \[ d = 2s = 2(6) = \mathbf{12\text{ cm}}. \]

question.en: In triangle \(PQR\), side \(p = 8\), side \(q = 11\), and side \(r = 13\). Find the exact value of \(\cos P\).
question.ar: In triangle \(PQR\), side \(p = 8\), side \(q = 11\), and side \(r = 13\). أوجد exact value of \(\cos P\).

solution.en:
Step 1: Apply the Law of Cosines for angle \(P\): \[ p^2 = q^2 + r^2 - 2qr\cos P \implies \cos P = \frac{q^2 + r^2 - p^2}{2qr}. \]

Step 2: Substitute given side lengths: \[ \cos P = \frac{11^2 + 13^2 - 8^2}{2(11)(13)} = \frac{121 + 169 - 64}{286} = \frac{226}{286} = \mathbf{\frac{113}{143}} \approx 0.7902. \]

question.en: A triangle has side lengths \(a = 5\), \(b = 6\), and \(c = 7\). Use Heron's formula to compute its exact area.
question.ar: حل المسألة التالية في (Lines, Triangles & Polygons): A triangle has side lengths \(a = 5\), \(b = 6\), and \(c = 7\). Use Heron's formula to compute its exact area.

solution.en:
Step 1: Compute semi-perimeter \(s\): \[ s = \frac{a + b + c}{2} = \frac{5 + 6 + 7}{2} = \frac{18}{2} = 9. \]

Step 2: Apply Heron's formula: \[ \text{Area} = \sqrt{s(s - a)(s - b)(s - c)} = \sqrt{9(9 - 5)(9 - 6)(9 - 7)} = \sqrt{9(4)(3)(2)} = \sqrt{216} = \mathbf{6\sqrt{6}} \approx 14.70. \]
